title: Eternal Wisdom, Thee We Praise
description: Eternal Wisdom, Thee We Praise in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 123 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God the Creator”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal Wis-dom, thee we praise; Thee all thy crea-tures sing: While with thy name, rocks, hills, and seas, And heaven's high pal-ace, ring.

lines: While with thy name, rocks, hills, and seas,
Thy hand, how wide it spread the sky!
Tinged with a blue of heavenly dye,
Thy glories blaze all nature round,
Through skies, and seas, and solid ground,
Our souls with vast amazement fill,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
